scene_translation: Descending the stairs, the air shifted to a cool stillness. Faint wartime writing remained etched on the concrete walls. You thought you heard footsteps approaching from the depths of the passage — but the man in grey was already standing there. "You came, Tesuto. This place... only your grandmother should have known about it." He spoke without turning around. There was no anger in his voice — only the quiet exhaustion of someone who had been waiting a very long time.
grammar_note: 【〜続ける】 attached to the stem of a verb, this means 'to keep doing' or 'to continue doing.' Here: 待ち続けた人 — 'a person who kept on waiting.' It emphasizes duration and persistence. Compare: 待った (waited) vs. 待ち続けた (kept waiting, waited on and on).

mystery_memo: The man in grey has now revealed himself as someone who knew the grandmother and was waiting for the player to find this place — he was guiding them all along. His tone suggests regret or grief rather than threat. The underground passage is the physical heart of the mystery. The notebook map led here precisely. The locker key's purpose is not yet clear — there may be something locked in this passage. The grandmother's connection to the man in grey is the next major reveal, approaching scene 9-10.
